display.purpose: The programme name in the hero, over the scrim. One per page.

headline.purpose: Major section headings. Secondary sections step down to clamp(1.75rem, 3.6vw, 2.5rem).

title.purpose: Curriculum entries, on-the-ground blocks, sub-headings. Faculty names sit at a fixed 1.4rem.

quote.purpose: The featured testimonial only. Supporting testimonials drop to 1.05rem body on paper/90.

numeral.purpose: The price, and only the price. The superseded rate sits beside it in ui at 1.5rem, struck through.

body.purpose: All running text, capped at the single 34rem (~68ch) measure.

body-large.purpose: Standfirst paragraphs directly under a section heading.

ui.purpose: Alegreya Sans wherever text is an instrument rather than a passage: nav, buttons, prices, captions, attributions, footer.
ui.note: Alegreya Sans ships a 0.175em word space against Arial's 0.278em, which reads as run-together words at nav and label sizes. Every sans usage must carry word-spacing: 0.09em.

label.purpose: Uppercase tracked name for an adjacent value (Dates, Included, To book). Never an eyebrow above a heading.

motion.name: ease-settle
motion.purpose: The only authored easing. Exponential ease-out used by the reveal (900ms) and the one-time hero scale (2000ms).

motion.name: duration-reveal
motion.purpose: Opacity, transform and blur on the curriculum reveal — the page's single authored moment.

motion.name: stagger-reveal
motion.purpose: Per-item delay across the curriculum list, applied via --reveal-delay.

motion.name: duration-hero-settle
motion.purpose: Hero photograph settling from scale(1.07) to scale(1), once, on load.

motion.name: duration-chrome
motion.purpose: Header ground/scrim crossfade, mobile anchor-row max-height + opacity, and the 4px arrow nudge on button hover.

motion.name: duration-disclosure
motion.purpose: Chevron rotation on the credits disclosure.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single conversion action — an email booking link. The pill shape is exclusive to it, so it is findable by shape alone.
components.html: Reserve a place
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; background: var(--color-pomegranate, #a32e38); color: #fff; font-family: var(--font-alegreya-sans), system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 500; word-spacing: 0.09em; text-decoration: none; padding: 14px 28px; border: none; border-radius: 9999px; transition: background-color 200ms, color 200ms; } .ds-btn-primary__arrow { width: 16px; height: 16px; transition: transform 500ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: var(--color-pomegranate-bright, #e2706b); color: var(--color-ink, #141110); } .ds-btn-primary:hover .ds-btn-primary__arrow { transform: translateX(4px); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-pomegranate-bright, #e2706b); outline-offset: 3px; border-radius: 9999px; }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: The one secondary route (a travel enquiry). Square-cornered and hairline-bordered so it can never be mistaken for the booking pill.
components.html: Ask us about travel
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; background: transparent; color: var(--color-paper, #f1ebe1); font-family: var(--font-alegreya-sans), system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; word-spacing: 0.09em; text-decoration: none; padding: 12px 24px; border: 1px solid var(--color-rule, #2e2822); border-radius: 0; transition: border-color 200ms; } .ds-btn-outline svg { width: 16px; height: 16px; color: var(--color-pomegranate-bright, #e2706b); } .ds-btn-outline:hover { border-color: var(--color-faint, #8a7f72); } .ds-btn-outline:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-pomegranate-bright, #e2706b); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Text Link
components.description: Inline link in running text. Underline is a faint hairline at 4px offset and is never removed — only recoloured on hover.
components.html: Places are booked by email — write to us and we will help you plan it.
components.css: .ds-prose { font-family: var(--font-alegreya), Georgia, serif; font-size: 1.0625rem; line-height: 1.7; color: var(--color-paper, #f1ebe1); max-width: 34rem; } .ds-link { color: inherit; text-decoration: underline; text-decoration-color: var(--color-faint, #8a7f72); text-decoration-thickness: 1px; text-underline-offset: 4px; transition: text-decoration-color 200ms, color 200ms; } .ds-link:hover { text-decoration-color: var(--color-pomegranate-bright, #e2706b); } .ds-link:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-pomegranate-bright, #e2706b); outline-offset: 3px; border-radius: 2px; }

components.name: Section Nav
components.description: The fixed header's anchor row in its settled state: ink at 92% with a backdrop blur and a hairline bottom border.
components.html:
Decolonial Dialogues
  • Programme
  • Faculty
  • Voices
  • What it costs
components.css: .ds-nav { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 24px; height: 4.5rem; padding: 0 32px; background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-ink, #141110) 92%, transparent); backdrop-filter: blur(12px); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--color-rule, #2e2822); font-family: var(--font-alegreya-sans), system-ui, sans-serif; word-spacing: 0.09em; } .ds-nav__mark { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; color: var(--color-paper, #f1ebe1); font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: -0.01em; text-decoration: none; transition: opacity 200ms; } .ds-nav__mark svg { width: 20px; height: 20px; color: var(--color-pomegranate-bright, #e2706b); } .ds-nav__mark:hover { opacity: 0.8; } .ds-nav__list { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 32px; list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; font-size: 0.875rem; } .ds-nav__list a { color: var(--color-muted, #a89b8c); text-decoration: none; transition: color 200ms; } .ds-nav__list a:hover { color: var(--color-paper, #f1ebe1); } .ds-nav__list a:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-pomegranate-bright, #e2706b); outline-offset: 3px; border-radius: 2px; }

components.name: Field Label and Value
components.description: The specification pattern. This is the system's replacement for an info card: uppercase tracked label above a body-scale value, over a hairline.
components.css: .ds-spec { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(2, minmax(0, 1fr)); gap: 32px; max-width: 32rem; margin: 0; padding-top: 40px; border-top: 1px solid var(--color-rule, #2e2822); } .ds-spec dt { font-family: var(--font-alegreya-sans), system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.14em; word-spacing: 0.09em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--color-muted, #a89b8c); } .ds-spec dd { margin: 8px 0 0; font-family: var(--font-alegreya), Georgia, serif; font-size: 1.0625rem; line-height: 1.7; color: var(--color-paper, #f1ebe1); }

components.name: Rule-Separated List Item
components.description: The recurring content unit and the system's stand-in for a card: a hairline above, 36px of breathing room, no box. Carries the page's one authored reveal on the curriculum.
components.html:
1. The history of modern colonialism

    From its beginnings in the conquest of Al-Ándalus to the present-day conflict in Palestine.

  2. Decolonizing knowledge and spirituality

    The theory of how knowledge itself was colonized.
components.css: .ds-ruled { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; } .ds-ruled li { border-top: 1px solid var(--color-rule, #2e2822); padding: 36px 0; } .ds-ruled li:first-child { border-top: 0; padding-top: 0; } .ds-ruled li:last-child { padding-bottom: 0; } .ds-ruled h3 { font-family: var(--font-alegreya), Georgia, serif; font-size: clamp(1.3rem, 2.1vw, 1.7rem); font-weight: 500; line-height: 1.08; letter-spacing: -0.018em; color: var(--color-paper, #f1ebe1); margin: 0; } .ds-ruled p { max-width: 34rem; margin: 16px 0 0; font-family: var(--font-alegreya), Georgia, serif; font-size: 1.0625rem; line-height: 1.7; color: var(--color-muted, #a89b8c); }

components.name: Feature Quote
components.description: The lead testimonial. Display face at quote scale on the raised band, attribution in the sans below.
components.css: .ds-quote { max-width: 56rem; margin: 0; padding: 32px; background: var(--color-ink-raised, #1c1815); } .ds-quote blockquote { margin: 0; font-family: var(--font-alegreya), Georgia, serif; font-size: clamp(1.45rem, 3vw, 2.15rem); font-weight: 500; line-height: 1.32; letter-spacing: -0.018em; text-wrap: balance; color: var(--color-paper, #f1ebe1); } .ds-quote figcaption { margin-top: 32px; font-family: var(--font-alegreya-sans), system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; word-spacing: 0.09em; color: var(--color-muted, #a89b8c); }

components.name: Ornament
components.description: The one decorative element: the pomegranate mark between two hairlines, marking the page's single held statement. Keep it rare.
components.css: .ds-ornament { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 16px; color: var(--color-pomegranate-bright, #e2706b); } .ds-ornament span { display: block; height: 1px; width: 64px; background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-faint, #8a7f72) 60%, transparent); } .ds-ornament svg { width: 28px; height: 28px; }

narrative.overview:
The page behaves like a Granadan courtyard opened at night: a warm, dark enclosure whose walls are photographs, whose light is a single column of warm paper-coloured type, and whose only ornament is a drawn pomegranate. Nothing is boxed. Sections are separated the way an arcade separates bays — by a hairline and a change of ground tone, never by a card, a panel or a shadow. The photographs are not illustrations sitting inside the layout; they are the layout's material, running edge to edge and taking type only over a gradient scrim.

The dark ground was chosen from the use scene, not from category habit: this page is mostly opened on a phone, in the evening, from an Instagram link. It is warm near-black rather than blue-black, pulled from the shadow values in the Granada photography the page is built on. The accent is pomegranate because Granada means pomegranate and the fruit is the city's own emblem — taken from the city's heraldry rather than from Alhambra tilework, so the motif reads as a mark rather than as pastiche.

The arrangement itself is a decision, not a default. Offered distinctive alternative worlds, the client chose the category standard — the familiar course page a visitor already knows how to read — and named Emergence Magazine and Orion as the quality bar. Everything here therefore spends its ambition on execution: generous typography, restrained density, large photography carrying the weight, and exactly one authored moment of motion in the whole page. Future surfaces inherit that stance; the convention is the brief, and the craft is the differentiator.
keyCharacteristics: Warm near-black ground (ink), never blue-black, never a light theme
One superfamily — Alegreya and Alegreya Sans — for display, body, and UI alike
Pomegranate as the single accent, in exactly two values
Full-bleed photography with gradient scrims; no framed or inset images
Hairline rules and tonal ground shifts instead of cards, panels, or shadows
Square corners everywhere except pill actions and circular portraits
One authored reveal in the entire page

rules.name: The Single Ember Rule
rules.body: Pomegranate is the only accent this system has, and it exists in exactly two values: the deep fill and the bright on-dark mark. Never introduce a second hue for state, category, emphasis, or "variety". If something needs to stand apart from muted text, it becomes paper — not a new colour.

rules.name: The Legibility Floor Rule
rules.body: Anything carrying text on the ink ground clears 4.5:1. This is not theoretical: faint was raised from #6d6357, which measured 3.2:1 and failed as text. Below that floor a value is decoration — a rule, a marker, an underline stroke — and may never be given words to carry.

rules.name: The Two-Ground Rule
rules.body: Depth comes from alternating ink and ink-raised bands with a hairline at the seam. That alternation is the whole sectioning vocabulary. A section that "needs" a card is a section that needs the other ground.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Alegreya and Alegreya Sans, and nothing else. Display and body are the same face at different sizes; the sans is the same superfamily. Do not pair in a third typeface for "contrast" — the contrast here is size and leading, not family. System display faces are out entirely.

rules.name: The Corrected Word Space Rule
rules.body: Alegreya Sans ships a 0.175em word space against Arial's 0.278em, which at nav and label sizes reads as run-together words. Every use of the sans therefore carries word-spacing: 0.09em — it is baked into both .ui and .label. There is no legitimate use of Alegreya Sans in this system without it.

rules.name: The One Measure Rule
rules.body: Every passage of running text is capped at 34rem (~68ch) via .measure. A paragraph wider than the measure is a bug, not a layout choice.

rules.name: The Label Is Not A Kicker Rule
rules.body: The uppercase tracked label is a name for an adjacent value — "Dates", "Included", "To book". It never appears above a heading as an eyebrow or category tag.

rules.name: The Full-Bleed Rule
rules.body: Photographs run to the edges of their section or fill a defined aspect well. They are never inset in a frame, never given a border, never rounded, and never captioned inside a box. The only exception is the circular faculty portrait.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: A 1px rule-coloured border is the only divider in the system: section seams, list separators, disclosure edges. No thick rules, no double rules, no decorative dividers other than the Ornament.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Depth is tone, scrim, and hairline. If an element seems to need a shadow to separate from its surroundings, it is on the wrong ground.

rules.name: The Scrim Rule
rules.body: Type is never set directly on a photograph. Any text over an image sits on a gradient or wash of the page ground, and the header carries its own top scrim whenever it is transparent over the hero — the Granada sky is bright enough to swallow a nav.

rules.name: The Square Corner Rule
rules.body: Radius 0 unless the element is an action pill or a portrait. A rounded card is a contradiction in this system twice over: it is a card, and it is rounded.

rules.name: The No Cards Rule
rules.body: No bordered boxes, no filled panels, no tiles. This is enforced, not aspirational — the Instagram panel was rebuilt from a bordered box into a hairline row to honour it. Content is separated by rules and grounds; if a group needs to feel distinct, give it a hairline above it and space around it.

rules.name: The One Moment Rule
rules.body: The page has exactly one authored reveal: the curriculum list, whose items rise 18px out of a 6px blur on a 900ms exponential ease-out, staggered 70ms apart. It was removed from every other section during the finish review, and that is the standing rule — motion elsewhere is state response only (hover colour, the 4px arrow nudge, the 500ms header settle, the 300ms chevron, the one-time 2000ms hero scale). Adding a second reveal does not double the effect; it destroys the first one.

rules.name: The Visible-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Content ships visible in the served HTML. The reveal is opted into by a pre-paint inline script that only hides elements once it has confirmed it can bring them back — gated on IntersectionObserver support and prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference, with a 1.5s watchdog that reveals anything still hidden. No-JS, reduced-motion, and failed-observer visitors get the whole page immediately. Any future motion must be built the same way round.

dos: Do keep pomegranate to its two values and to a small share of any screen. Deep (#a32e38) fills the booking action; bright (#e2706b) carries every small mark on the dark ground.
Do clear 4.5:1 on the ink ground for anything carrying words. faint was raised from #6d6357 (3.2:1) for exactly this reason; treat that as the floor, not the target.
Do ship word-spacing: 0.09em with every use of Alegreya Sans — it is already in .ui and .label, and any new sans rule must carry it too.
Do cap running text at the single 34rem measure (~68ch).
Do separate content with a hairline and a change of ground tone.
Do put a gradient scrim under any type that sits over a photograph.
Do draw new icons at 1.4 stroke on a 24×24 viewbox, fill: none / stroke: currentColor, to match the set.
Do route every image through the Photo primitive so it inherits its blur placeholder, its ink-sunk well, and its intrinsic dimensions.
Do keep the pill shape exclusive to the booking action, so the single conversion route is findable by shape alone.
donts: Don't add a card, a bordered box, a filled panel, or a tile. The Instagram panel was rebuilt from a box into a hairline row to hold this line.
Don't add a box-shadow. There are none in this system; depth is tone, scrim, and hairline.
Don't round anything that is not the booking pill or a portrait.
Don't introduce a third typeface, or a system display face. One superfamily, two sizes of idea.
Don't use a unicode glyph, emoji, or icon font anywhere. Icons are authored SVG, including the disclosure marker — the native <details> triangle is suppressed on purpose.
Don't set the uppercase tracked label as an eyebrow or kicker above a heading. It names an adjacent value or nothing.
Don't add a second authored motion.
Don't invert to a light ground or shift to a blue-black. The warmth is pulled from the photography and the darkness is chosen for a phone in the evening.
Don't let a photograph render without a placeholder or an explicit aspect — a white flash or a reflow on this page reads as a broken page, because the photography is the material.
